messages:
jordan: Heads-up — follow-up on the continuous-batching scheduler refactor. want to align on queue lifecycle, admission signals, and eviction semantics before i draft the RFC.

maya: good call. main risk i see is lifecycle flapping during deploys (queues created/destroyed rapidly). causes KV cache churn and spikes in tail latency.

liam: agreed. also head-of-line blocking when a tenant has a long-running streaming session — blocks coalescing for other small reqs.

sasha: for lifecycle, can we decouple queue existence from active inflight? create queue object on first route bind, but keep tombstone for Xs before GC.

jordan: +1. tombstone window solves thundering restarts. what's a safe default? 30s?

maya: 30s might be low for slow rollouts. i'd say 5m for safety, but make it configurable per env.

liam: note: longer tombstone increases memory usage and KV cache retention — tradeoff vs rewarm cost.

devops-bot: deploy: continuous-batcher/v2 promoted to staging — running canary with queue-tombstone=300s

sasha: for admission signals, propose two-layer: soft credits for throughput shaping + hard tokens for tenant concurrency cap.

jordan: elaborate on soft vs hard — how are they enforced in practice? eviction vs backpressure?

sasha: soft credits: shared pool, algorithm tries to maximize packing but will preempt small batches after deadline. hard tokens: refuse enqueue if tokens exhausted (fast failure).

maya: need graceful fallback. if hard token denies, return 429 with Retry-After and hint to use lower concurrency. don't OOM queue.

liam: important: we must surface metrics: enqueue_denied_count, soft_preempt_count, tombstone_recreate_rate, kv_rewarm_seconds. ops needs these for SLA tuning.

jordan: agreed. also add per-tenant hint for expected seq_len distribution so runtime can pick kernel family and batch window.

sasha: that should be opt-in. not every consumer can annotate. use historical histogram as fallback.

maya: eviction policy options: fifo_soft (evict oldest soft credit holder), tail_drop (deny new small requests), priority_weighted (prefer short-latency routes). which to default?

liam: default= fifo_soft seems safest for fairness. priority_weighted can be advanced opt-in for internal tenants.

jordan: operationally, we need escape hatches: 1) admin kill queue, 2) force-evict tenant, 3) dynamic tombstone shrink. add to console.

sasha: UX note: admin kill should trigger graceful drain of in-flight, not abrupt GPU kill. add abort-after-ms flag.

maya: perf test plan: synthetic mix 80% short (<=32 tokens), 20% long (streaming). run with tombstone=30s vs 5m and compare warmup penalty.

liam: also test with KV cache warmup disabled to measure worst case. capture tail 99.9 and p999 latency.

jordan: OK action items: maya write perf matrix + run tests, sasha draft admission API (soft/hard tokens + metrics), liam add observability dashboards, i'll stub RFC and coordinate.

sasha: throwing a quick config prototype:

```yaml
batcher:
  tombstone_seconds: 300
  soft_pool_size: 1024
  hard_tokens_per_tenant: 64
  eviction_policy: "fifo_soft"
  admit_deadline_ms: 12
```

maya: looks good. maybe make hard_tokens scalable by tenant_tier.

devops-bot: note: perf job queued: cb-refactor-perf-run-1715001145

jordan: timeline: aim to have perf results and admission API draft by EOW. RFC end of next week. if anyone blocked ping me.

liam: ack — i'll start dashboard stubs now.

maya: ack, will kick off perf runs.

sasha: ack, will push admission draft to PR and link.

jordan: thanks team :thumbsup:
